rationale:
The proof should be split. It has four separate obligations: a measure-theoretic one (Fubini and the FTC on the unit cube), a differential-calculus one (pulling dγ back along an affine cube as a divergence), their combination into Stokes for one cube, and finite integer bookkeeping.

The split is also forced by a pipeline constraint. Commits 14cdd14d8 and fa0865963 record the Ch07 leaf gate (check_source_delta): a leaf may append exactly ONE theorem, with no imports, helpers or set_option, within the default 200k heartbeats. So step 3 of the supplied proof, as written, cannot be carried out by a leaf. The split uses the supplied proof's own parenthetical alternative instead: Fubini in the other coordinates plus the FTC in the i-th one, each tool of which is reachable.

subproblems.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus in one coordinate on the open unit cube of Euclid (k+1)
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, i ∈ Fin (k+1), and let G : Euclid (k+1) → ℝ be C¹. Write Q^d := {y ∈ Euclid d : 0 < y_j < 1 for all j} (Lebesgue measure) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid k, let insertNth i c y' ∈ Euclid (k+1) be the point (toLp ∘ Fin.insertNth i c ∘ ofLp) with i-th coordinate c and remaining coordinates y' in order. Then y ↦ DG(y)e_i is integrable on Q^{k+1}, and ∫_{Q^{k+1}} DG(y)e_i dy = ∫_{Q^k} G(insertNth i 1 y') dy' − ∫_{Q^k} G(insertNth i 0 y') dy'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 1)) (G : Euclid (k + 1) → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → IntegrableOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) {y : Euclid (k + 1) | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1} ∧ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (k + 1) | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = (∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i (1 : ℝ) (WithLp.ofLp y)))) - ∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.insertNth i (0 : ℝ) (WithLp.ofLp y)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (“Divergence theorem on the unit cube … Equivalently: for each i, Fubini in the other m coordinates and the fundamental theorem of calculus in the i-th coordinate”), specialised to a single coordinate i and a single C¹ function G. Mathlib's box divergence theorem is in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem, which the frozen Ch07 contract does NOT import, and a leaf may not add imports. So the parent's parenthetical Fubini + FTC route is the one written out here. Every tool below is reachable from the frozen imports.

Notation. For d ∈ ℕ, Q^d := {y ∈ Euclid d | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, and B^d := Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1) ⊆ (Fin d → ℝ) is the open box. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For c ∈ ℝ and z : Fin k → ℝ, insertNth i c z : Fin (k+1) → ℝ has i-th coordinate c and (succAbove i l)-th coordinate z l. toLp = WithLp.toLp 2 and ofLp = WithLp.ofLp are mutually inverse, and (toLp x) j = x j.

1. Regularity. G is C¹, so G is differentiable everywhere (ContDiff.differentiable, 1 ≠ 0) and y ↦ fderiv ℝ G y is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Hence g(y) := fderiv ℝ G y e_i is continuous on Euclid (k+1).
2. Integrability (first conjunct). Q^{k+1} ⊆ toLp '' Icc 0 1, because y = toLp (ofLp y) and 0 ≤ y j ≤ 1. toLp '' Icc 0 1 is compact: it is the image of the compact box Icc 0 1 under the continuous map toLp. A continuous function is integrable on a compact set (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact), hence on the subset Q^{k+1} (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
3. Transport to coordinates. For every n and every f : Euclid n → ℝ, ∫_{Q^n} f = ∫_{B^n} f(toLp x) dx. Indeed toLp : (Fin n → ℝ) → Euclid n is a measure-preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp) measurable embedding (MeasurableEquiv.toLp), and toLp ⁻¹' Q^n = B^n, so MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb applies. Apply this to the three integrals of the claim. Using ofLp (toLp z) = z, the claim becomes
   ∫_{B^{k+1}} g(toLp x) dx = ∫_{B^k} G(toLp(insertNth i 1 z)) dz − ∫_{B^k} G(toLp(insertNth i 0 z)) dz.
4. Splitting off coordinate i. Let e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i : (Fin (k+1) → ℝ) ≃ᵐ ℝ × (Fin k → ℝ). Its inverse is (t, z) ↦ insertNth i t z (piFinSuccAbove_symm_apply, Fin.insertNthEquiv), and e.symm is measure-preserving (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, .symm). Moreover e.symm ⁻¹' B^{k+1} = Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k: insertNth i t z lies in the box iff t ∈ (0,1) and every z l ∈ (0,1) (Fin.forall_iff_succAbove). So ∫_{B^{k+1}} g(toLp x) dx = ∫_{Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k} h, where h(t, z) := g(toLp(insertNth i t z)) and the measure is volume = volume.prod volume.
5. Fubini. h is continuous on ℝ × (Fin k → ℝ) (Continuous.finInsertNth, continuity of toLp and of g). Hence h is integrable on the compact set Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1, and therefore on Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k. By Measure.prod_restrict, (volume.prod volume).restrict (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k) = (volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1)).prod (volume.restrict B^k), so h is integrable for this product measure. Fubini with the second factor outside (integral_prod_symm) gives ∫_{Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k} h = ∫_{z ∈ B^k} (∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} h(t, z) dt) dz.
6. FTC in the i-th coordinate. Fix z and put φ(t) := G(toLp(insertNth i t z)). Then toLp(insertNth i t z) = toLp(insertNth i 0 z) + t • e_i. Check coordinates: at i both sides equal t; at succAbove i l both equal z l, since e_i vanishes there (Fin.succAbove_ne). So t ↦ toLp(insertNth i t z) has derivative e_i, and by the chain rule φ'(t) = fderiv ℝ G (toLp(insertNth i t z)) e_i = h(t, z). This is continuous in t, hence interval integrable, and intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt gives ∫_0^1 h(t, z) dt = φ(1) − φ(0). Since 0 ≤ 1, the interval integral is the integral over Ioc 0 1 (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). That equals the integral over Ioo 0 1 (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo; singletons are null). So ∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} h(t, z) dt = G(toLp(insertNth i 1 z)) − G(toLp(insertNth i 0 z)).
7. Conclusion. For c ∈ {0, 1}, z ↦ G(toLp(insertNth i c z)) is continuous, hence integrable on Icc 0 1 ⊇ B^k. By integral_sub, ∫_{B^k} G(toLp(insertNth i 1 z)) dz − ∫_{B^k} G(toLp(insertNth i 0 z)) dz = ∫_{B^k} (G(toLp(insertNth i 1 z)) − G(toLp(insertNth i 0 z))) dz. By step 6 and setIntegral_congr_fun (B^k is measurable), this equals ∫_{z ∈ B^k} ∫_{t ∈ Ioo 0 1} h(t, z) dt dz. By steps 3–5, that is the transported left-hand side. This proves the second conjunct.
   For k = 0, Fin 0 → ℝ is a single point and B^0 is all of it, so every step applies verbatim. ∎
proof_key_steps: G ∈ C¹, so g = DG(·)e_i is continuous. Q^{k+1} lies in the compact set toLp '' [0,1]^{k+1}, so g is integrable on Q^{k+1}.
Transport the three cube integrals to open boxes in Fin d → ℝ with the measure-preserving embedding toLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp).
Split off coordinate i with the measure-preserving map (t, z) ↦ insertNth i t z (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove). The box pulls back to Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ B^k.
Fubini (Measure.prod_restrict, integral_prod_symm) for the continuous integrand, with the integral over t inside.
FTC in t: toLp(insertNth i t z) = toLp(insertNth i 0 z) + t e_i, so d/dt G(…) = DG(…)e_i and ∫_{(0,1)} = G(…1…) − G(…0…).
Recombine with integral_sub (continuous integrands on the compact closure) to get the face difference.

subproblems.title: Exterior derivative along an affine coordinate cube equals the divergence of its coefficient field
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P arbitrary, a ∈ Euclid P, and let γ : Euclid P → Covector(Euclid P, m) be a C¹ m-form. Put Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (y ∈ Euclid (m+1)), E := (e_{ι(j)})_{j∈Fin(m+1)}, and for i ∈ Fin (m+1), F_i(y) := (−1)^i γ(Φ(y))(e_{ι(succAbove i l)})_{l∈Fin m}. Then every F_i is C¹, and for every y ∈ Euclid (m+1): dγ(Φ(y))(E) = Σ_i DF_i(y)(e_i), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and d is SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (a : Euclid P) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m), ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → (∀ i : Fin (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y : Euclid (m + 1) => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * γ (a + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)))) ∧ ∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), exteriorDerivative γ (a + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), fderiv ℝ (fun z : Euclid (m + 1) => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * γ (a + ∑ j, z j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ))) y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (“dγ as a divergence … By SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply (removeNth i v = v ∘ succAbove i) and the chain rule (DΦ_p(y)e_i = e_{ι(i)}): dγ(Φ_p y)(E_p) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[γ(·)(E_p∘succAbove i)](Φ_p y)(e_{ι(i)}) = Σ_i ∂_i G_i(y)”). Here the integer base point toLp(b) is generalised to an arbitrary point a ∈ Euclid P, and ι is arbitrary (no monotonicity is used). The C¹ claim (a) is that step's remark “G is C^∞”, stated for C¹ forms.

Notation. w_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 ∈ Euclid P. Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y j • w_j. E := (w_j)_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)}. For i ∈ Fin (m+1), E∘succAbove i = (w_{succAbove i l})_{l ∈ Fin m} = (fun l => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1). F_i(y) := (−1)^i · γ(Φ y)(E∘succAbove i). e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Euclid (m+1).

1. Φ is affine. Let L := Σ_j (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight w_j : Euclid (m+1) →L[ℝ] Euclid P. Then L v = Σ_j v j • w_j and Φ = a + L. Hence Φ is C¹ (contDiff_const.add L.contDiff), and HasFDerivAt Φ L y for every y (L.hasFDerivAt.const_add a). Also L e_i = Σ_j (e_i) j • w_j = w_i, since (e_i) j = 1 if j = i and 0 otherwise.
2. (a) Regularity. For a fixed tuple v ∈ (Euclid P)^m, the evaluation ω ↦ ω v is the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v. So y ↦ γ(Φ y)(E∘succAbove i) equals (apply (E∘succAbove i)) ∘ γ ∘ Φ. This is a composition of C¹ maps (γ by hypothesis, Φ by step 1), so it is C¹. Multiplying by the constant (−1)^i keeps it C¹ (contDiff_const.mul). Hence every F_i is C¹.
3. (b) Exterior derivative. γ is C¹, hence differentiable at x := Φ y. By SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative_apply (Mathlib extDeriv_apply), exteriorDerivative γ x E = Σ_i (−1 : ℤ)^i • fderiv ℝ (fun x' => γ x' (Fin.removeNth i E)) x (E i). Here Fin.removeNth i E = E∘succAbove i by definition, and E i = w_i.
4. Chain rule. Put g_i(x') := γ x' (E∘succAbove i). Since γ has a derivative at x, so does g_i (HasFDerivAt.continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const). Write D_i := fderiv ℝ g_i x. Since F_i = (−1)^i · (g_i ∘ Φ), HasFDerivAt.comp with step 1 and then HasFDerivAt.const_mul give HasFDerivAt F_i ((−1)^i • D_i.comp L) y. Hence fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i = (−1)^i · D_i (L e_i) = (−1)^i · D_i w_i.
5. Summation. The ℤ-scalar action (−1 : ℤ)^i • r equals the real product (−1 : ℝ)^i · r (zsmul_eq_mul with the cast of (−1)^i). So by step 4 the i-th term in step 3 equals fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i. Summing over i gives exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = Σ_i fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i for every y ∈ Euclid (m+1). Together with (a), this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ(y) = a + L y, where L v = Σ_j v_j e_{ι(j)} is a continuous linear map. Φ is C¹ with DΦ ≡ L, and L e_i = e_{ι(i)}.
F_i = (−1)^i · ev_{E∘succAbove i} ∘ γ ∘ Φ is C¹, since evaluation is ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply, a continuous linear map.
exteriorDerivative_apply: dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[γ(·)(removeNth i E)](Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}), with removeNth i E = E∘succAbove i.
Chain rule: DF_i(y)e_i = (−1)^i D[γ(·)(E∘succAbove i)](Φ y)(L e_i) = (−1)^i D[…](Φ y)(e_{ι(i)}). Sum over i, converting the ℤ-action (−1)^i • to real multiplication.

subproblems.title: Stokes formula for one oriented lattice unit cube
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P arbitrary, b ∈ ℤ^P, and let γ be a C¹ m-form on Euclid P. Put Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E := (e_{ι(j)})_j. For i ∈ Fin (m+1) let E'_i := (e_{ι(succAbove i l)})_{l∈Fin m} and define the front and back faces Φ¹_i(y') := toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} and Φ⁰_i(y') := toLp(b) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)}, where 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1 ∈ ℤ^P. With Q^d the open unit cube of Euclid d: ∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ(y))(E) dy = Σ_{i∈Fin(m+1)} (−1)^i (∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ¹_i(y'))(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ⁰_i(y'))(E'_i) dy').

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (“Cubical Stokes”) of the parent proof, with its ingredients from steps 1–3. Here ι is arbitrary (no monotonicity is used) and γ is only assumed C¹. The analytic ingredients are two sibling theorems: cube_partial_ftc (Submission.cmcdtfrcb_cube_partial_ftc, the per-coordinate Fubini + FTC form of step 3) and pullback_divergence (Submission.cmcdtfrcb_pullback_divergence, step 2).

Notation. a := toLp(fun k => (b k : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P. w_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1. Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y j • w_j for y ∈ Euclid (m+1), and E := (w_j)_j. For i ∈ Fin (m+1): E'_i := (EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1)_{l ∈ Fin m} and F_i(y) := (−1)^i · γ(Φ y)(E'_i). For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, ι^c_i(y') := toLp(insertNth i c (ofLp y')) ∈ Euclid (m+1). The front face has base point toLp(fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)); the back face has base point a. Q^d is the open unit cube of Euclid d.

1. Divergence form. Apply pullback_divergence to (P, m, ι, a, γ) with the hypothesis γ ∈ C¹. It gives (a) each F_i is C¹, and (b) exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = Σ_i fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i for all y. Rewriting the left-hand integrand with (b) gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ y)(E) dy = ∫_{Q^{m+1}} Σ_i fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i dy.
2. Interchange of sum and integral. For each i, apply cube_partial_ftc to (k, i, G) := (m, i, F_i), using F_i ∈ C¹ from step 1(a). Its first conjunct says that y ↦ fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i is integrable on Q^{m+1}. Hence integral_finsetSum (deprecated alias: integral_finset_sum) gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} Σ_i fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i dy = Σ_i ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i dy. It remains to show, for each fixed i, that ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i dy equals the i-th summand of the right-hand side.
3. Per-coordinate FTC. The second conjunct of the same instance of cube_partial_ftc gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ F_i y e_i dy = ∫_{Q^m} F_i(ι^1_i y') dy' − ∫_{Q^m} F_i(ι^0_i y') dy'.
4. Faces of a face (step 1 of the parent proof). For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m:
   a + Σ_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)} (ι^c_i y') j • w_j = a + c • w_i + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1.
   To see this, split the sum at i (Fin.sum_univ_succAbove _ i) and use (ι^c_i y') i = c (Fin.insertNth_apply_same) and (ι^c_i y') (succAbove i l) = y' l (Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove). Also toLp(fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) = a + w_i: at k = ι i both sides are b_k + 1, and at k ≠ ι i both are b_k. With c = 1 (one_smul), Φ(ι^1_i y') is the front-face point toLp(fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1. With c = 0 (zero_smul, add_zero), Φ(ι^0_i y') is the back-face point a + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1.
5. Constants. By step 4, F_i(ι^1_i y') = (−1)^i · γ(front point)(E'_i) and F_i(ι^0_i y') = (−1)^i · γ(back point)(E'_i). Pull (−1)^i out of both integrals (integral_const_mul) and factor (mul_sub). The difference in step 3 becomes (−1)^i · (∫_{Q^m} γ(front point)(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(back point)(E'_i) dy'), which is the i-th summand of the claim.
6. Summing over i (step 2) proves the identity. For m = 0 every step applies unchanged: Q^0 = Euclid 0 is a single point of volume 1, and the face integrals are evaluations at vertices. ∎
proof_key_steps: pullback_divergence with a = toLp(b): each F_i is C¹, and dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i DF_i(y)e_i pointwise.
Integrability from cube_partial_ftc (first conjunct) allows ∫ Σ_i = Σ_i ∫ (integral_finsetSum).
cube_partial_ftc (second conjunct): ∫_{Q^{m+1}} DF_i e_i = ∫_{Q^m} F_i(insertNth i 1 ·) − ∫_{Q^m} F_i(insertNth i 0 ·).
Face identity: Φ(insertNth i c y') = toLp(b) + c e_{ι(i)} + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)}, and toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) = toLp(b) + e_{ι(i)}.
Pull out (−1)^i (integral_const_mul) and sum over i.

subproblems.title: Integer regrouping of the signed faces of a lattice n-chain into a lattice (n−1)-chain
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P strictly increasing and b ∈ ℤ^P, and let β assign an integer to each pair. Then there are a finite set s' of pairs q = (ι', b') with ι' : Fin m → Fin P strictly increasing and b' ∈ ℤ^P, and integers β'_q, such that for every function I from pairs (ι', b') to ℝ: Σ_{p∈s} β_p Σ_{i∈Fin(m+1)} (−1)^i (I(ι∘succAbove i, b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) − I(ι∘succAbove i, b)) = Σ_{q∈s'} β'_q I(q), where 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (β : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℤ), (∀ p ∈ s, StrictMono p.1) → ∃ (s' : Finset ((Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (β' : (Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℤ), (∀ q ∈ s', StrictMono q.1) ∧ ∀ I : (Fin m → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → ℝ, ∑ p ∈ s, (β p : ℝ) * ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (I (p.1 ∘ Fin.succAbove i, p.2 + Pi.single (p.1 i) 1) - I (p.1 ∘ Fin.succAbove i, p.2)) = ∑ q ∈ s', (β' q : ℝ) * I q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 (“Regrouping”) of the parent proof, together with the strict-monotonicity remark of its step 1. It is stated for an arbitrary real-valued function I on index pairs, so one choice of (s', β') serves every test form at once. Here 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1 ∈ ℤ^P.

1. Index set. Let A := s ×ˢ Finset.univ, the finite set of pairs a = (p, i) with p ∈ s and i ∈ Fin (m+1). For a = ((ι, b), i) put front(a) := (ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i, b + Pi.single (ι i) 1), back(a) := (ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i, b) and c(a) := β (ι, b) · (−1)^i ∈ ℤ.
2. Choice of s' and β'. Put s' := A.image front ∪ A.image back, a finite set of pairs whose first component is Fin m → Fin P. Define β'(q) := Σ_{a ∈ A, front a = q} c(a) − Σ_{a ∈ A, back a = q} c(a) ∈ ℤ (sums over Finset.filter).
3. Strict monotonicity. Let q ∈ s'. Then q = front(a) or q = back(a) for some a = ((ι, b), i) ∈ A, so (ι, b) ∈ s and q.1 = ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i. By hypothesis ι is strictly increasing, and Fin.succAbove i is strictly increasing (Fin.strictMono_succAbove). So their composition is strictly increasing.
4. Expansion of the left-hand side. Fix I. Distribute β_p over the inner sum (Finset.mul_sum) and the sign over the difference. Rewrite the double sum over p ∈ s and i ∈ Fin (m+1) as a sum over A (Finset.sum_product). Casting gives (c(a) : ℝ) = (β p : ℝ) · (−1 : ℝ)^i (push_cast). So LHS = Σ_{a ∈ A} c(a) · I(front a) − Σ_{a ∈ A} c(a) · I(back a) (Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ring).
5. Fibrewise regrouping. Let g ∈ {front, back}. g maps A into s' (Finset.mem_image_of_mem, then the left or right part of the union). By Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to, Σ_{a ∈ A} c(a) · I(g a) = Σ_{q ∈ s'} Σ_{a ∈ A, g a = q} c(a) · I(g a). On the fibre over q, I(g a) = I(q), so the inner sum is (Σ_{a ∈ A, g a = q} c(a) : ℝ) · I(q) (Int.cast_sum, Finset.sum_mul).
6. Conclusion. Subtracting the two regrouped sums (Finset.sum_sub_distrib) gives LHS = Σ_{q ∈ s'} ((Σ_{front a = q} c a : ℝ) − (Σ_{back a = q} c a : ℝ)) · I(q). This equals Σ_{q ∈ s'} (β'(q) : ℝ) · I(q), since the cast of an integer difference is the difference of the casts (push_cast, ring). Steps 2, 3 and 6 give the required s' and β'. ∎
proof_key_steps: A := s × Fin (m+1), with front(a) = (ι∘succAbove i, b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}), back(a) = (ι∘succAbove i, b) and c(a) = β_p(−1)^i.
s' := front(A) ∪ back(A), β'(q) := Σ_{front a = q} c(a) − Σ_{back a = q} c(a).
q.1 = ι∘succAbove i is StrictMono by the hypothesis and Fin.strictMono_succAbove.
LHS = Σ_A c·I∘front − Σ_A c·I∘back (sum_product). Regroup each sum by fibres (sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to) and subtract.
